author: gkswns0531
body:
I would like to sincerely thank the MS GraphRAG team for creating such an outstanding project. It’s truly impressive, and I’ve been very eager to use it myself. However, since the environment I work in is based entirely on ElasticSearch, I ran into compatibility limitations with the existing vector store options. To address this, I implemented ElasticSearch support myself and am submitting this PR in the hope that it can be merged into the main project.


## Description

Adds ElasticSearch vector store support to GraphRAG following the existing LanceDB implementation pattern. Enables enterprise organizations with ElasticSearch infrastructure to use GraphRAG without additional vector databases.

## What's Implemented

- **`ElasticSearchVectorStore`**: Complete `BaseVectorStore` interface implementation
- **Factory Integration**: Added to `VectorStoreFactory` with `elasticsearch` type
- **Enterprise Features**: KNN search, bulk operations, dynamic vector dimensions
- **Full Compatibility**: Zero breaking changes, works alongside existing stores


## Testing

- **11 integration tests** - 100% pass rate
- **Validated**: Real GraphRAG indexing/search workflows


## Usage

```yaml
vector_store:
  default_vector_store:
    type: elasticsearch
    url: "http://localhost:9200"
    es_index_name: "graphrag_entities"
```

## Files Changed

- `graphrag/vector_stores/elasticsearch.py` (+217 lines) - Core implementation
- `tests/integration/vector_stores/test_elasticsearch.py` (+315 lines) - Tests  
- `graphrag/vector_stores/factory.py` (+4 lines) - Factory integration
- `pyproject.toml` (+1 line) - Dependency

## Impact

- **No Breaking Changes**: Existing code continues to work
- **Enterprise Ready**: Leverages existing ElasticSearch infrastructure
- **Production Tested**: Validated with real GraphRAG workflows

## Related Issues
#2001

body:
Description
This PR updates the transitive dependency golang.org/x/oauth2 to version v0.30.0 to mitigate a high-severity vulnerability (https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-6v2p-p543-phr9) identified via terratest → go-getter → oauth2.

Vulnerability Details
Vulnerable Library: golang.org/x/oauth2@v0.7.0
CVE ID: [CVE-2025-22868](https://proxy.golang.org/golang.org/x/oauth2/@v/v0.7.0.zip)
Severity: High (CVSS 7.5)
Impact: An attacker can pass a malformed token to exhaust memory during parsing, potentially causing Denial of Service (DoS).
Publish Date: 2025-02-26
Remediation: Upgrade to golang.org/x/oauth2@v0.30.0 or later.

Fix Applied
Updated golang.org/x/oauth2 to v0.30.0 via go get.
Verified compatibility and ran tests to ensure no breaking changes were introduced.

body:
## Summary

The test assertion became incorrect as it seems that an integration was [made available](https://github.com/elastic/integrations/pull/14591) for versions `>=9.1.0`: 
```javascript
{
    icon: '/api/fleet/epm/packages/cloud_asset_inventory/1.0.0/img/logo_cloud_security_posture.svg',
    id: 'cloud_asset_inventory',
    score: 80,
    title: 'Cloud Asset Discovery',
    type: 'integration',
    url: '/app/integrations/detail/cloud_asset_inventory/overview'
}
```
The integration contains the `discover` string in title, which is what the test is looking for. Integrations are fetched via an API and they are defined in the integration repository. 

This test should **NOT** check for the length of results as they might change.

The following assertion:
```javascript
expect(results[0].title).to.be('Discover')
``` 
should always succeed as this is a direct match, which means the result has the highest score and will always appear on top. Eventually this test could be improved to exclude integrations.

Closes: #228679

#### Issue
Some users had reported that they were unable to download their training files in bulk upload. Investigation showed that it was linked to unusual characters in their training notes. 

#### Work done
- Updated `toCSV` function to use the same conversion as other areas of codebase for training notes

#### Note
This matches the way notes are converted in the codebase, as notes are escaped before saving to the database, and are unescaped using the `unescape` function in the training class. However, it's not ideal using escape before saving to the database. The function itself was deprecated due to inconsistencies in how it parses strings, but also there's not much of a use case for escaping it as it is just a text field.

All notes are saved in this format so it would be a big job to change this set up and this is the easiest solution for now.

body:
## The Issue

- #41

It would be nice to be able to easily adjust the varnish startup parameters.
Env-Variables are a bit more intuitive than docker compose file creation.
Further I think it would be beneficial to increase the default varnishd limits for http headers and payload sizes.
These payloads often are larger on development environments and can cause hard to track issues.

## How This PR Solves The Issue

Adds a env-variable for the parameters and defines larger limits by defaiult.

## Manual Testing Instructions

```bash
ddev add-on get https://github.com/CandoImage/ddev-varnish/tarball/20250721_das-peter_41_provide-env-var-to-set-varnishd-parameters
ddev dotenv set .ddev/.env.varnish --varnish-varnishd-params='-p http_max_hdr=12345'
ddev restart
ddev varnishadm param.show http_max_hdr
```

## Automated Testing Overview

Added new test to check if customization is picked up:
`bats ./tests/test.bats --filter "customize varnishd startup parameters" `

body:
## #️⃣ 연관된 이슈

> closes #90 

## 📝 작업 내용
이번 PR은 “팔로워 리스트 조회 API #77”과 로직 구조가 매우 유사하여, 리팩토링 중심으로 작업을 진행하였습니다. 주요 변경 사항은 다음과 같습니다:

1. **CursorBasedList 도입**
대부분의 조회 기능이 무한 스크롤 기반으로 동작하기 때문에, 커서 기반 페이징 방식이 적절하다고 판단하였습니다. 이에 따라 커서 기반 페이징 처리를 표준화하고자 CursorBasedList를 도입하였으며, 관련 상세 내용은 노션에 정리해두었으니 참고 부탁드립니다.
2. **QueryProjection 기반 공통 DTO 적용**
Querydsl의 @QueryProjection을 활용하면 공통 응답 DTO를 생성하는 데 유용하다는 점을 확인하여, 이번에 유사한 조회 로직들에 적용해보았습니다.
FollowQueryDto는 팔로워 및 팔로잉 사용자 정보를 모두 담을 수 있는 구조로 설계되어 있으며, 응답 형식의 차이는 주로 followerCount 포함 여부입니다.
따라서, 쿼리 결과는 FollowQueryDto로 통일하여 받아오고, 서비스 계층에서 필요한 응답 DTO로 변환하는 방식으로 구성해 조회 로직의 재사용성과 응집도를 높였습니다.
3. **MapStruct 도입**
서비스 계층에서 FollowQueryDto를 실제 응답 DTO로 변환하는 작업을 명확하게 분리하고자 MapStruct를 도입하였습니다.
기존에는 조회 DTO → 응답 DTO 변환 책임이 응답 DTO나 서비스 클래스 중 한 곳에 맡아 혼용되고 있었고, 이는 의존성 침해 및 서비스 로직 복잡도 증가라는 단점이 있었습니다.
이러한 문제를 해소하고자 명확한 매핑 책임을 가진 Mapper 클래스를 분리하여 도입하였고, 이를 통해 매핑 로직을 간결하고 명시적으로 관리할 수 있게 되었습니다.

앞으로 다른 조회 API 개발 시에도, 공통 필드는 QueryDto로 분리하고, 매핑에는 MapStruct를 활용하는 구조를 적용하면 유지보수성과 일관성을 높일 수 있을 것으로 기대합니다. 감사합니다.

## 📸 스크린샷

## 💬 리뷰 요구사항

현재 조회 dto(`FollowQueryDto`) -> 응답 dto(`UserFollowingResponse`)를 파싱하는 매퍼 (`FollowMapper`)를 application하위에 mapper 패키지를 만들어서 두었는데 이 위치에 대한 부분도 한번 확인 부탁드릴게요!


### 📌 PR 진행 시 이러한 점들을 참고해 주세요

    * P1 : 꼭 반영해 주세요 (Request Changes) - 이슈가 발생하거나 취약점이 발견되는 케이스 등
    * P2 : 반영을 적극적으로 고려해 주시면 좋을 것 같아요 (Comment)
    * P3 : 이런 방법도 있을 것 같아요~ 등의 사소한 의견입니다 (Chore)

# Proposal to fix two issues related to the URL bar:

## Issue 1: 
Solving #35, collapse extension identity box in URL bar. This fixes the overly large identity box when using extensions such as Bonjourr.

## Issue 2: 
On some devices, the center aligned text in the URL bar causes weird visual problems and weird cursor placement, especially when not using `gwfox.plus`. These problems are fixed by left aligning the text in the URL bar as is default in Firefox. 

I understand that the center aligned URL bar is a key visual part of this CSS. In order to retain this, but give the option to left align the text, I have created a new `about:config` variable that is default set to `false`. When set to `true`, the text in the URL bar will be left aligned, fixing some visual issues for some users.

author: copilot
body:
## Problem

The tests in `test_train_lstm_script.py` and `test_lstm_trainer.py` were checking for the existence of `.json` files after model saving operations, making them fragile and implementation-dependent. These tests would break if the mock implementation changed its file format, even though the actual checkpoint saving functionality remained correct.

**Problematic code:**
```python
# test_train_lstm_script.py line 169
assert Path(checkpoint_path + '.json').exists()  # Mock save creates .json file

# test_lstm_trainer.py line 590  
assert os.path.exists(save_path + '.json')
```

## Solution

Replaced implementation-dependent file format checks with tests that verify the actual behavior we care about:

1. **Checkpoint Manager Tests**: Now verify that checkpoint operations complete successfully and that files exist in either format (`.pth` for real PyTorch or `.json` for mock), making tests robust to implementation changes.

2. **Model Save/Load Tests**: Now test the complete save/load cycle to ensure the interface contract works, regardless of the underlying file format.

**After:**
```python
# Implementation-agnostic checkpoint verification
expected_best_path = Path(self.temp_dir, 'best_model.pth')
assert (expected_best_path.exists() or 
        Path(str(expected_best_path) + '.json').exists())

# Save/load cycle testing
try:
    trainer.save_model(save_path, include_metadata=True)
    trainer.load_model(save_path, load_optimizer=True)
    save_load_success = True
except Exception:
    save_load_success = False
assert save_load_success
```

## Benefits

- **Robustness**: Tests work regardless of save implementation (PyTorch vs mock, .pth vs .json)
- **Intent-focused**: Tests verify actual checkpoint behavior rather than implementation details
- **Maintainable**: Mock implementation changes won't break tests
- **Zero regression**: All 49 existing tests continue to pass

## Validation

- ✅ All original tests pass (49/49)
- ✅ Save-related tests pass (6/6) 
- ✅ No breaking changes to functionality
- ✅ Demonstrated robustness to implementation changes

Fixes #84.

author: copilot
body:
## Problem

The inference engine was using a problematic nested class workaround to bypass weight initialization when loading pre-trained LSTM models:

```python
# Problematic workaround in inference_engine.py
class MockLSTM(SteelDefectLSTM):
    def _init_weights(self):
        pass  # Skip weight initialization

self.lstm_model = MockLSTM(lstm_config)
```

This approach had several issues:
- Creates temporary subclasses just to override initialization
- Not reusable across the codebase
- Unclear intent and poor maintainability
- Violates clean code principles

## Solution

Added a clean, parameter-based solution by introducing a `skip_init_weights` parameter to `SteelDefectLSTM.__init__()`:

```python
# New clean approach
self.lstm_model = SteelDefectLSTM(lstm_config, skip_init_weights=True)
```

### Key Changes

1. **Added `skip_init_weights` parameter** to `SteelDefectLSTM.__init__()`
   - Optional parameter defaults to `False` for full backward compatibility
   - When `True`, skips weight initialization for efficiency when loading pre-trained weights
   - Clear documentation explains the use case

2. **Enhanced weight initialization robustness**
   - Fixed handling of 1D vs 2D tensors to prevent initialization errors
   - Improved error handling for bias parameters and different tensor dimensions

3. **Removed nested class workaround**
   - Eliminated `MockLSTM` class from inference engine
   - Replaced with explicit parameter usage
   - Much cleaner and more maintainable code

### Usage Examples

```python
# Default behavior (unchanged)
model = SteelDefectLSTM(config)

# Skip initialization when loading pre-trained weights
model = SteelDefectLSTM(config, skip_init_weights=True)
model.load_state_dict(checkpoint['model_state_dict'])
```

## Benefits

- ✅ **Cleaner code**: No more inheritance-based workarounds
- ✅ **Maintainable**: Explicit parameter control vs hidden behavior  
- ✅ **Documented**: Clear documentation on when and why to use the parameter
- ✅ **Reusable**: Can be used anywhere in the codebase that needs to skip initialization
- ✅ **Efficient**: Avoids unnecessary weight initialization when loading pre-trained models
- ✅ **Backward compatible**: All existing code continues to work unchanged

## Testing

- Created comprehensive tests validating both `skip_init_weights=True` and `skip_init_weights=False`
- Verified backward compatibility with existing code
- Tested edge cases including state dict loading and forward pass functionality
- Validated complete inference engine workflow simulation

Fixes #92.

author: whatever125
body:
## Changes
1. I2C Bus Initialization Fix
Properly deinit pins before reinitialization to prevent GPIO reservation conflicts. Added `i2c_common_deinit_pins()` before `i2c_common_set_pins()`
2. NULL Buffer Protection in ISR
Added safety check in `i2c_isr_receive_handler` for NULL data buffers. Early return when `i2c_operation->data == NULL` (occurs during NACK scenarios). Prevents `StoreProhibited` panic when `i2c_ll_read_rxfifo` attempts to write to NULL
- Condition occurs when:
  - NACK received (`I2C_LL_INTR_NACK` sets status to `I2C_STATUS_ACK_ERROR`)
  - ISR still attempts FIFO read despite no valid buffer
  - Fix safely handles this edge case without data loss (FIFO empty during NACK)

author: copilot
body:
The LSTMTrainer constructor was being called with an incomplete configuration that caused runtime errors when PyTorch is available.

## Problem

In `scripts/train_lstm_model.py`, the LSTMTrainer was initialized with only the LSTM model configuration section:

```python
lstm_config = config['lstm_model']  # Only contains architecture, training, loss_function
trainer = LSTMTrainer(model, lstm_config, device)  # Missing required sections
```

However, LSTMTrainer expects a complete configuration with these sections:
- `training` - Training parameters 
- `optimization` - Optimizer configuration
- `scheduler` - Learning rate scheduler settings
- `loss_function` - Loss function configuration
- `early_stopping` - Early stopping parameters
- `logging` - Logging and checkpointing settings

This mismatch caused the trainer to use empty dictionaries for missing sections, leading to runtime errors when PyTorch attempts to initialize components.

## Solution

Modified the script to construct a proper training configuration by:

1. **Extracting existing sections** from `lstm_config`: `training`, `loss_function`
2. **Adding required sections** with sensible defaults: `optimization`, `scheduler`, `early_stopping`, `logging`
3. **Preserving configuration values** like early stopping patience from the original LSTM config

```python
# Create training configuration for LSTMTrainer
training_config = {
    'training': lstm_config.get('training', {}),
    'loss_function': lstm_config.get('loss_function', {}),
    'optimization': {
        'optimizer': 'adam',
        'beta1': 0.9,
        'beta2': 0.999,
        'epsilon': 1e-8
    },
    'scheduler': {
        'type': 'reduce_on_plateau',
        'factor': 0.5,
        'patience': 5,
        'min_lr': 1e-6
    },
    'early_stopping': {
        'enabled': True,
        'patience': lstm_config.get('training', {}).get('early_stopping_patience', 15),
        'min_delta': 1e-4,
        'monitor': 'val_loss',
        'restore_best_weights': True
    },
    'logging': {
        'tensorboard_enabled': True,
        'csv_logging': True,
        'log_interval': 10,
        'save_interval': 5
    }
}

trainer = LSTMTrainer(model, training_config, device)
```

## Validation

- ✅ Configuration structure now matches LSTMTrainer expectations
- ✅ All required sections present with proper values  
- ✅ Existing configuration values preserved and correctly extracted
- ✅ No breaking changes to other parts of the codebase
- ✅ Existing tests continue to pass

Fixes #85.

Lowers the overheads of UDF calls in most cases by avoiding unnecessary conversion to dataframes.

I see almost 2x speedup with the benchmark code I ran on my local Mac (single core):

```python
import bodo.pandas as bd
import time
import pandas as pd

N = 50_000_000
df = pd.DataFrame({"hours": pd.date_range("1980-01-01", periods=N, freq="s")})
bdf = bd.from_pandas(df)
start = time.perf_counter()
new_S = bdf.hours.dt.year
new_S.execute_plan()
print("Bodo UDF took", time.perf_counter() - start, "seconds")
```

This PR adds comprehensive unit tests for the `cp_cluster-helper.R` functions, specifically addressing the edge cases mentioned in issue #108.

## Changes Made

Created a new test file `tests/testthat/test-cp_cluster-helper.R` with **32 passing tests** that cover:

### Functions Tested

1. **`.get_prop_bs_by_cp_tbl_data_list_filter_above_min`** - Tests the critical zero-row handling logic:
   - Zero-row reconstruction when filtering results in empty data frames
   - Proper column handling (batch/stim columns vs other columns) during reconstruction
   - NA value handling and attribute preservation
   - Empty input and single-row edge cases

2. **`.get_prop_bs_by_cp_tbl_data_list_filter_cyt_pos`** - Tests filtering behavior:
   - Conditional filtering based on `filter_other_cyt_pos` parameter
   - Proper handling of the last element in the list
   - Named result preservation and attribute handling

3. **`.get_cp_cluster_dens_tbl_get_actual_ind_early_return`** - Tests early return structure:
   - Correct tibble structure creation with 512 x-columns
   - NA value population across all density columns
   - Vector input processing (taking first elements)

### Key Edge Cases Addressed

The tests specifically target the problematic scenarios mentioned in the issue:

- **Zero-row reconstruction**: When `nrow(x_out) == 0` in the filter function, ensuring proper data frame reconstruction with batch/stim columns preserved and other columns set to NA
- **Early return conditions**: Testing the 512-column tibble creation with proper NA handling
- **Attribute preservation**: Ensuring `n_cell` and other attributes are maintained through operations

### Test Design

The tests are designed to:
- Work independently without requiring full package loading
- Use mock helper functions to isolate the functions under test
- Provide meaningful assertions about data structure and content
- Cover both normal operation and edge cases

All tests pass successfully and provide robust coverage of the edge cases that were identified as problematic in the original issue.

Fixes #108.

When asked to parse a level beyond the last existing level, we parse
the last existing level instead as a recovery.

The implementation of the warning in this PR always says "level
<unknown>", this should be improved before a merge can be considered.

Also perhaps instead of changing the grammar files we should
autodetect these single-anonymous-level entries to be RIGHTA? When
there is only 1 level RIGHTA is the only sensible option AFAICT.

We should probably also reject left and right recursive notations in
constr level 0 (cf the various test suite occurrences of the warning),
level 0 is meant to be atomic.

This pull request introduces several updates to enhance dependency management, improve code quality, and modernize the codebase. Key changes include configuring Dependabot for automated dependency updates, integrating Simplycop for RuboCop rules, and modernizing syntax and dependencies for Ruby 3.2+ compatibility.

### Dependency Management Enhancements:
* Added a Dependabot configuration (`.github/dependabot.yml`) to automate updates for Bundler and GitHub Actions dependencies on a daily schedule.
* Updated the gemspec (`rulezilla.gemspec`) to require Ruby 3.2+ and replaced `add_runtime_dependency` with `add_dependency` for `ostruct`. Added Simplycop as a development dependency.

### Code Quality Improvements:
* Updated `.rubocop.yml` to inherit Simplycop rules for performance, RSpec, and general linting.
* Regenerated `.rubocop_todo.yml` with updated RuboCop version and adjusted exclusions for new offenses, including `CustomCops/DefineMethod` and `RSpec/RemoveConst`.

### Syntax Modernization:
* Replaced deprecated `&block` syntax with `&` in method definitions in `lib/rulezilla/dsl.rb`.
* Updated symbol handling for `instance_variable_set` and `Object.const_set` to use modern Ruby syntax (e.g., `:@record` and `:DummyRule`). Changes applied across `lib/rulezilla/dsl.rb`, `spec/features/step_definitions/rulezilla_dsl_framework_steps.rb`, and `spec/spec_helper.rb`. body:
<!-- If this PR closes a JIRA ticket, make sure the title starts with the JIRA issue number,
for example JP-1234: <Fix a bug> -->
Resolves [JP-3866](https://jira.stsci.edu/browse/JP-3866)

<!-- If this PR closes a GitHub issue that is not attached to a Jira ticket, uncomment the line below, and reference it here by its number -->
Closes #9122 

<!-- describe the changes comprising this PR here -->
This PR updates `source_catalog` to use photutils methods instead of maintaining its own separate code where applicable.  This reduces technical debt, consolidating code so it needs to be maintained in just one place.  Changes include:

- Use `photutils.detection.core._StarFinderKernel` for DAOFind kernel handling
- Use `photutils.detection.daofinder._DAOStarFinderCatalog` methods for sharpness and roundness computation
- Use `photutils.segmentation.SourceCatalog.sky_centroid` method instead of keeping a JWST one
- Use `photutils.background.LocalBackground` to replace `JWSTSourceCatalog._aper_local_background`.  The computation of the local background itself appears to be identical between the two methods, but the former does not compute the error on the background value, which is needed by the source catalog.  Therefore I added a photutils-like median RMS estimator.  In a perfect world, this could get added into photutils later.
- Added unit test of the values of `xcentroid`, `ycentroid`, `sharpness`, `roundness`, `aper_bkg_flux`, and `aper_bkg_flux_err`.  The regtests also ensure the values are identical, but it's better to have "instant feedback" from the unit test while developing.

Changes that were considered but rejected include:

- Use astropy units conversions to do photometric conversions.  Making the change did not appear to appreciably reduce the amount of code needed.  IMO the main benefit of using astropy would be the ability to handle multiple different input/output units, which is not very relevant for the pipeline.

body:
### Description of work

This PR covers the GUI work for configuring Alerts.

### Ticket

The requirements are defined [here](https://github.com/ISISComputingGroup/IBEX/issues/8731)

### Acceptance criteria

- The GUI code should build from the command prompt (..\build\build.bat)
- The GUI should provide an easy and intuitive mechanism to configure alert details.
- The GUI should give ability to change the block level alert values after selecting the block.
- The GUI should give a separate section to see and alter the global alert values (emails, mobiles and message).
- The emails and mobiles should be first shown masked and remain so unless they are changed.

author: apognu
body:
This PR implements auto-assignments for cases. The exact details can be found in Linear, but overall:

 * A license entitlement enables case auto-assignment
 * An org can set a maximum size for the case backlog per user, per inbox
 * An inbox can enable auto-assignment
 * An inbox user can be added to an inbox rotation
 * A new endpoint can be used by a user to declare they are not available until a set date

Whenever elligible actions are performed, a task is enqueues that is going to run the algorithm to assign non-assigned, non-closed cases to available users, if their queue has slots. Those actions, for now are:

 * A case is created
 * A case is closed

The oldest case is assigned to the users with the least open, assigned cases, and so on until either all cases are assigned or there are no available slots in the available user's queues.

---

TODO:

 - [ ] Improve unavailability API: right now, it only asks for an end date and sets the unavailability to `[now()-end]`. I think we might want to do better than that, even if that is a good first use case. Changing the end date is possible until the period is passed, and cancelling the unavailability moves the end date to `now()`.
 - [ ] Add more hook points to trigger auto-assignment

body:
**Description:** 
--------------
This PR implements the foundational data structures and utility functions needed for Operational Transformation (OT) in the collaborative editor. 

**Changes:**

*   Added `constants/operationTypes.js` defining INSERT, DELETE, and RETAIN operations
*   Implemented `utils/operationUtils.js` with core functions:
    *   `createOperation()` for creating standardized operation objects
    *   `composeOps()` for combining sequential operations
    *   `invertOp()` for creating inverse operations (undo capability)
*   Added `utils/transform.js` with transformation functions:
    *   `transformOp()` for transforming operations against each other
    *   `transformPosition()` for adjusting cursor positions

**Why is this valuable?** 

This PR lays the groundwork for true real-time collaboration by implementing the core algorithms that will ensure consistency across multiple users editing simultaneously. The OT system will allow us to:

*   Maintain a consistent document state across all clients
*   Support concurrent editing without conflicts
*   Enable proper cursor tracking and visualization

**Resources and References**

[Basics of Operational Transformation](https://dev.to/sudoboink/the-basics-of-operational-transformation-288j)

**Test Plan:**

*   Tested with various operation combinations and edge cases
*   Verified mathematical properties of OT (convergence, intention preservation)

author: salavey13
body:
⚡: Feat: Улучшение SOS-флоу с геолокацией и динамической оплатой

[The Architect's Log: New intel received. The Captain's insights on the SOS flow are precise. The current implementation is too rigid. A truly Vibe-compliant system must be dynamic, responsive, and offer meaningful choices. The proposed geotag-first approach with variable pricing is strategically superior. It introduces a layer of realism and gamification. Re-architecting the SOS command module to integrate `user_states` for location capture before presenting payment options. The system will now calculate, not just assume.]

Капитан, твои замечания — чистая правда. Мы мыслим в одном направлении. Давай разберем по пунктам и реализуем next-level версию SOS-флоу.

### Анализ и План Действий

1.  **"Сценарии" vs. "Действия"**
    *   Ты прав, в event-based мире это почти одно и то же. **Сценарий** — это просто *последовательность Действий*. Наша тестовая страница позволяет вручную выполнять эту последовательность. "Автоматический оркестратор" был бы следующим шагом, где мы бы написали скрипт, который сам нажимает кнопки в нужном порядке и проверяет результат. Пока что наш ручной симулятор — это то, что нужно.

2.  **Создание аренды при оплате**
    *   Твоя логика абсолютно верна для реального мира. **Rental record должен создаваться только после оплаты "интереса"**. Наш `carRentalHandler` уже так и делает: он запускается *после* успешной оплаты и только *тогда* создает запись в таблице `rentals`. Так что здесь мы на правильном пути, ничего менять не нужно.

3.  **Улучшенный SOS-флоу (Гео-первый, Оплата-второй)**
    *   **Проблема:** Текущий SOS предлагает фиксированные цены без контекста.
    *   **Новая Логика:**
        1.  Пользователь нажимает `/sos`.
        2.  Бот отвечает: "Понял, нужна помощь. Сначала отправь свою геолокацию, чтобы я рассчитал стоимость и оповестил ближайших." Пользователь переводится в состояние `awaiting_sos_geotag`.
        3.  Пользователь отправляет геолокацию.
        4.  Система "рассчитывает" стоимость (пока что просто на основе простого правила) и предлагает 2-3 варианта оплаты (`50 XTR`, `200 XTR`, и т.д.) через reply-клавиатуру. *Состояние пользователя меняется на `awaiting_sos_payment_choice`*.
        5.  Пользователь выбирает опцию.
        6.  Система выставляет счет (инвойс).
        7.  После оплаты, `carRentalHandler` создает `sos_fuel` событие, куда в `payload` уже включены и координаты, и уплаченная сумма.
    *   **Реализация:**
        *   Добавим поле `hq_location` в таблицу `crews`, чтобы хранить координаты штаб-квартиры.
        *   Обновим `/sos` команду и добавим обработчик `handleLocationMessage` для состояния `awaiting_sos_geotag`.
        *   Обновим `carRentalHandler` для обработки платежей `sos_fuel` и `sos_evac`.

### Предоставленный Код:

#### 1. SQL Миграция: Добавляем `hq_location` в `crews`

Примени этот SQL-код к своей базе. Он добавит новое поле для хранения координат и обновит существующую команду, чтобы добавить демо-координаты

#### 2. Обновление Логики Команд и Обработчиков

Я переписал команду `/sos`, обработчики в `command-handler` и `telegramWebhook`, а также `carRentalHandler`, чтобы реализовать новый, умный флоу.

**Файлы (5):**
- `supabase/migrations/20240722100000_add_hq_location_to_crews.sql`
- `app/webhook-handlers/commands/sos.ts`
- `app/api/telegramWebhook/route.ts`
- `app/webhook-handlers/commands/command-handler.ts`
- `app/webhook-handlers/car-rental.ts`

author: copilot
body:
This PR implements support for negative (!) and double negative (!!) operators in DDOM template expressions, as requested in the issue.

## Changes Made

### Core Implementation
- **Added `UNARY_NOT` pattern** in `detection.ts` to detect `!` and `!!` operators at the start of expressions
- **Enhanced template evaluation** in `evaluation.ts` to handle unary NOT operators with proper precedence
- **Improved ternary condition handling** to recursively evaluate complex conditions including NOT operators

### Key Features
- Single NOT operator: `'${!this.$isActive}'` returns `'false'` when `$isActive` is truthy
- Double NOT operator: `'${!!this.$value}'` returns `'true'` or `'false'` based on truthiness
- Works in complex expressions: `'${!this.$flag ? "inactive" : "active"}'`
- Compatible with DOM elements: `textContent: '${!!this.$isVisible}'`

## Examples

```javascript
const spec = {
  $isActive: true,
  $count: 5,
  
  // Basic NOT operations
  negated: '${!this.$isActive}',        // 'false'
  boolean: '${!!this.$count}',          // 'true'
  
  // In ternary expressions
  status: '${!this.$isActive ? "inactive" : "active"}',    // 'active'
  hasItems: '${!!this.$count ? "has items" : "empty"}',    // 'has items'
  
  // In DOM elements
  document: {
    body: {
      children: [{
        tagName: 'div',
        textContent: '${!!this.$isActive}',                 // 'true'
        className: '${!this.$isActive ? "hidden" : "visible"}' // 'visible'
      }]
    }
  }
};
```

## Testing
- Comprehensive test suite covering all use cases
- Tests for simple NOT operations, complex ternary expressions, and DOM element usage
- All existing tests continue to pass (156/159 - same 3 unrelated failures as before)

Fixes #46.

### Docker Compose Files

  - Prometheus monitoring and Grafana dashboards

```python
client = MCPStoutClient(api_key="your-key")

#### Python SSE Client (`python_sse_client.py`)

async for chunk in client.stream_generate(prompt="Write a story"):

author: copilot
body:
This PR implements the archetype selection feature as requested in the issue. After sub-genre selection, users are now taken to a new archetype selection step where they can choose multiple character archetypes for their story.

## Key Features

### Two-Section Layout
- **Typical Archetypes**: Shows archetypes commonly associated with the selected sub-genre (loaded from the genre data)
- **Other Available Archetypes**: Shows all remaining archetypes in alphabetical order with descriptions

### Multiple Selection Support
- Users can select multiple archetypes via checkboxes (unlike previous single-selection steps)
- Selected archetypes are visually highlighted and stored in the story data
- Manual "Complete Story Selection" button to finish the process

### Updated Flow
The user flow has been updated from:
1. Story Type → 2. Subtype → 3. Key Theme → 4. Core Arc → 5. Genre → 6. Sub-Genre → **Story Complete**

To:
1. Story Type → 2. Subtype → 3. Key Theme → 4. Core Arc → 5. Genre → 6. Sub-Genre → **7. Archetype Selection** → Story Complete

## Implementation Details

- **Story class**: Added support for multiple archetype selections with methods to get typical vs other archetypes
- **New route**: `/archetype-selection` with GET/POST handlers for displaying and processing archetype selections
- **Template**: New `archetype_selection.html` with responsive grid layout and checkbox functionality
- **Session management**: Updated to store and load archetype selections
- **Save/Load**: JSON export/import now includes the `selected_archetypes` array

## Example Story Data
```json
{
  "story_type_name": "The Quest",
  "subtype_name": "Object Quest", 
  "key_theme": "The journey is as important as the destination.",
  "core_arc": "Trust forged under pressure.",
  "genre_name": "Fantasy",
  "sub_genre_name": "Urban Fantasy",
  "selected_archetypes": [
    "Hidden Mage",
    "Skeptic Detective", 
    "Loyal Companion"
  ]
}
```

The implementation correctly shows typical Urban Fantasy archetypes (Hidden Mage, Skeptic Detective, Fae Trickster) in the first section, with all other 105 archetypes available in the second section.

![Screenshot of archetype selection page](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/be6f3de2-596b-4f59-a78a-a4bdb318754c)

Fixes #68.

body:
## 📱 Mobile Responsiveness Improvements

This PR implements comprehensive mobile responsiveness enhancements for the SparkTest application's sidebar and dropdown components, transforming the mobile user experience from cramped and unusable to sleek and intuitive.

### 🎯 Key Features Implemented

#### **Mobile-First Sidebar Design**
- **Hamburger Menu**: Added responsive navigation button that appears on mobile devices (< 768px)
- **Collapsible Sidebar**: Transforms from fixed 64px desktop width to hidden off-screen mobile layout
- **Slide-Out Navigation**: Mobile sidebar slides in from left with full-width text labels and proper touch targets
- **Smart Overlay**: Click-to-dismiss overlay with proper z-index management

#### **Responsive Layout Architecture**
- **Context-Based State Management**: Created `SidebarProvider` for shared mobile menu state between components
- **Breakpoint-Aware**: Seamless layout switching using Tailwind's responsive utilities
- **Smooth Transitions**: Added CSS animations for sidebar open/close interactions

#### **Enhanced User Experience**
- **Desktop**: Compact sidebar (64px) with hover tooltips
- **Mobile**: Full navigation menu (256px) with readable text labels
- **Tablet**: Automatic responsive behavior at 768px breakpoint
- **Touch-Optimized**: Improved button sizing and spacing for mobile interaction

#### **Dropdown Optimization**
- **Search Dropdown**: Properly positioned and sized for small screens
- **Create Menu**: Responsive button layout with mobile-friendly spacing
- **Accessibility**: Maintained ARIA labels and semantic structure

### 📱 Tested Screen Sizes
- ✅ iPhone SE (320×568px)
- ✅ iPhone Standard (375×667px) 
- ✅ iPhone Pro Max (414×812px)
- ✅ iPad/Tablet (768×1024px)
- ✅ Desktop (1024px+)

### 🔧 Technical Implementation
- **Minimal Code Changes**: Surgical modifications preserving existing functionality
- **Context Pattern**: Shared state management between header and sidebar components
- **Performance**: Efficient re-renders and smooth animations
- **Type Safety**: Full TypeScript support with proper interfaces

### 📸 Visual Results

**Before - Mobile Issues:**

author: mytherin
body:
This PR adds support for checkpointing in-memory tables. Previously checkpoints were only performed for on-disk tables. Checkpoints serve two purposes for in-memory tables:

* This allows for vacuuming of deleted rows, allowing space to be reclaimed after deletes/truncation
* This allows for compression of in-memory tables, saving space

By default, vacuuming is enabled and compression of in-memory tables is disabled. Compression can be enabled on attaching using the `COMPRESS` flag:

```sql
ATTACH ':memory:' AS memory_compressed (COMPRESS)
```

Automatic checkpointing is determined using the `checkpoint_threshold`. However, since there is no WAL to track, we use a separate heuristic: the total committed sizes of all undo buffers. If this exceeds the `checkpoint_threshold`, a checkpoint is triggered. Manual checkpoints can also be triggered using the `CHECKPOINT` command.

author: oliver-sanders
body:
Revert the `--flow` behaviour changes on the group-trigger branch and replace it with something which maintains the previous behaviour for unconnected groups, but 

You might want to review this with `?w=1` on the end of the URL (hide whitespace changes in the force-trigger implementation)

#### New Behaviour

It should trigger tasks within their flow if available, else all flows.

* N=0 tasks already have a flow assigned.
* N!=0 tasks do not yet have a flow assigned.

When we are triggering n!=0 tasks, there is no appropriate flow to run them
in (this would involve flow merge prediction), so we default to all active
flows as the least objection ate default.

Before group trigger, we triggered tasks independently, i.e. we assumed
there were no dependencies between the tasks and ran them all
simultaneously. With the group trigger extension, we enhanced trigger to
make it aware of interdependent tasks.

Triggering independent tasks (pre group-trigger behaviour):
  * If we trigger a n=0 task, we leave it in the flow it is already in.
  * If we trigger a n!=0 task, we default to all active flows.

Triggering interdependent tasks (group trigger extension):
  If the list of tasks being triggered contains any interdependent tasks,
  we treat these interdependent tasks as a group.

  * If we trigger a group which contains n=0 tasks, the whole group should
    be triggered using the set of flows possessed by these n=0 tasks.
  * If we trigger a group which does not contain n=0 tasks, we default to
    all active flows.

author: shaneknapp
body:
this supersedes https://github.com/cal-icor/jupyterhub-k8s-node-placeholder/pull/13

sometimes `ical` is unable to reach the public calendar, and this results in a cascading (but very brief) failure:

```
niquests.exceptions.HTTPError: 500 Server Error: Internal Server Error for url: https://calendar.google.com/calendar/ical/c_35d90f50598c1472a4154c538bb49a21eabd8be93831d7de345d53fea8e19390%40group.calendar.google.com/public/basic.ics
```

after this happens, `niquests.get_url()` throws the above with the `requests.raise_for_status()` call and emits the following bit in to the logs:

```
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "<frozen runpy>", line 198, in _run_module_as_main
  File "<frozen runpy>", line 88, in _run_code
  File "/srv/scaler/__main__.py", line 4, in <module>
    main()
  File "/srv/scaler/scaler.py", line 86, in main
    calendar = get_calendar(config["calendarUrl"])
```

after this, the `node-placeholder-scaler` pod crashes, and immediately restarts (cascading failures but ultimately benign and self-healing.  yay k8s!).

however, there are GCP alerts set up to scan the calendar entries for HTML (meaning someone formatted text in the scaler event description).  this check simply looks for `<` or `>`, and the `<frozen runpy>` error matches this (natch!).  

this change was proposed by @ryanlovett in the aforementioned PR at the top of this desc, but due to git silliness his PR touches more than it should.

author: lfryemason
body:
The `progress-table-v2-default-v2` DCDO flag was meant to change whether a user who had not ever selected the toggle to view the v2 would see the v1 or v2 progress page by default. This logic was not working because the server was sending back `null` for both `false` and unset values. We had no way to determine whether a user had clicked the toggle or was seeing the page for the first time.

This PR fixes that issue by changing from a boolean value for `showProgressV2` on the user setting to a string value with either `legacy` or `v2`. Now, we can check if the user has set `legacy` or if the value is null.

This will have a side effect of wiping any current settings and will one-time default all users to the v2 view. This is expected and helpful based on our progress deprecation plan. See [thread](https://codedotorg.slack.com/archives/C06ERUABG01/p1752861115719289).

## Summary

- Adds a simple, native Kubernetes `autoscaling/v2` HorizontalPodAutoscaler configuration
- Targets the `k8bit-test-nodejs-app` deployment with standard scaling parameters
- CPU utilization threshold: 70%
- Replica range: 2-10 pods
- Basic scale up/down behavior for production workloads

## Purpose

This PR provides a baseline HPA configuration that any Node.js developer would create for their application. The configuration is intentionally simple and follows Kubernetes best practices.

**K8bit Integration**: This native HPA will be detected by K8bit, which can then analyze the workload and calculate appropriate ScaleOps recommendations and policies to enhance the scaling behavior with AI-driven optimizations.

## Configuration Details

The HPA configuration includes:
- **Resource Metrics**: CPU utilization targeting 70% average
- **Scaling Behavior**: 
  - Scale up: 50% increase or 2 pods max per minute
  - Scale down: 25% decrease or 1 pod max per minute  
  - Conservative stabilization windows (60s up, 300s down)
- **Standard Labels**: `app: k8bit-test-nodejs-app` for workload identification

## Testing

To test the HPA:
```bash
kubectl apply -f k8s/hpa.yaml
kubectl get hpa k8bit-test-nodejs-app-hpa
```

author: mullertremolo
body:
Unescapes the unicode escapes found in the JavaScript `jsSlug` to fix the `/f/` slug URL that is created on Bunkr streaming API pages.

Without this fix, files names with a character that Bunkr escaped would be shown as getting a 404 because we requested the wrong URL.

Example:

```js
var jsSlug = 'a-\u0026-b-BMvk2CDL.mp4';
```

Before: `https://bunkr.cr/f/a-%5Cu0026-b-BMvk2CDL.mp4`
After: `https://bunkr.cr/f/a-&-b-BMvk2CDL.mp4`

author: benjamn
body:
After attempting to write the description for my PR #7934, I thought it might be helpful to break those changes up into separate PRs, as mentioned in https://github.com/apollographql/router/pull/7934#issuecomment-3097080630.

This PR contains just the internal unification of the `NamedSelection` enum into a struct of the same name. All the existing parsing logic has been updated to generate an AST in the new format, so no changes to parsing behavior are necessary, and no version gating is needed.

Of course, this change of representation triggered a whole bunch of snapshot updates, which I've kept in their own commit for ease of reviewing.

The first part of the #7934 description is still accurate/appropriate for this PR:

> Builds on PR #7933 as well as transitive dependencies including PRs #7932 and #7927, all targeting the `benjamn/JSONSelection-abstract-types` branch from PR #7926.
>
> This PR implements a significant simplification to the JSONSelection ~formal EBNF grammar and~ parser implementation, based around the insight that `NamedFieldSelection` was essentially a single-`Key` `NamedPathSelection`, so it makes sense to represent them in a common way, rather than representing/handling them separately. Internally, the `NamedSelection` enum has become a struct that always has a `path: PathSelection` field, so we can reuse all the usual `PathSelection` and `PathList` machinery for every kind of `NamedSelection` element. This internal refactoring was possible without changing the grammar, since the new `NamedSelection` struct represents the previous grammar's AST structure in the same way it represents the new grammar's simplified structure.
>
> Technical note: besides `path`, the other field of the new `NamedSelection` struct is `prefix: NamingPrefix`, where `NamingPrefix` is a private enum type that can represent the no-prefix case (`NamingPrefix::None`), the `Alias` case (`NamingPrefix::Alias(Alias)`), as well as a `NamingPrefix::Spread(Option<Range<usize>>)` variant, which is currently used to represent the former `PathWithSubSelection ::= Path SubSelection` case as `NamingPrefix::Spread(None)`, since existing behavior dictates the `SubSelection` gets inlined/spread into the larger selection, even without the `...` syntax that we're planning to introduce soon. Once we do introduce the explicit `...` spread operator, we can represent that with `NamingPrefix::Spread(Some(start..end))` where the range identifies the location of the `...` token in the source, when present. Of course we don't want there to be a functional difference between `NamingPrefix::Spread(None)` and `::Spread(Some(_))` (both get spread), but tracking the optional range of the `...` token seemed useful for tooling.

author: dmontgomery
body:
`System.ArgumentException: A PostgreSQL type with the name 'bookings.stream_message' was not found in the current database info at Npgsql.Internal.NpgsqlDatabaseInfo.GetPostgresType(DataTypeName dataTypeName) `

This is caused by the Npgsql internal info cache not getting updated after initial database creation.  Previously, restarting the app a second time would work successfully because the info cache could see the user defined type for the booking.stream_message on the second run.  Simple fix is to force the info cache to reload after database initialization

author: janusw
body:
This PR implements a workaround for mono/SkiaSharp#2550 in the context of MAUI 9.

The SkiaSharp bug did already occur with MAUI 8, and was a bit easier to work around there (see #2820 by @inforithmics). It transformed a bit with MAUI 9 (see https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/issues/2550#issuecomment-3094137132), and the old workaround stopped working.

Gladly, an effective workaround for MAUI 9 was found by @SimonvBez, and I adapted and applied it to Mapsui.UI.Maui.MapControl (extending the previous MAUI 8 workaround).

Note: In order to include Android-specific code properly (via conditional compilation, `#if ANDROID ... #endif`), it was necessary to add a net9.0-android TFM to Mapsui.UI.Maui.

A reproducer (based on Mapsui.Samples.Maui) can be found here:
* https://github.com/janusw/Mapsui/tree/SkiaSharp_issue2550_repro/Samples/Mapsui.Samples.Maui
* https://github.com/janusw/Mapsui/commit/f149bb322396c5fa20c8dfc40e71cff84433a6a5

I verified that it is fixed with this PR (on a Pixel 9 with Android 16).

@SimonvBez If you have any comments on this, please let us know.

## Summary
- Introduced a new `pkg/output` package that centralizes all console output logic
- Replaced scattered `fmt.Printf` calls throughout the codebase with structured output methods
- Improved consistency and maintainability of console output across all commands

## Changes

### New Output Package
Created `pkg/output` with:
- **Writer interface**: Defines standard output operations (Info, Warning, Error, Success, etc.)
- **ConsoleWriter**: Implementation with ANSI color support and configurable log levels
- **Progress components**: Spinner and progress bar implementations for better UX
- **Helper functions**: Colorize, FormatBold, FormatHighlight for consistent formatting

### Refactored Files
Updated all main command files to use the new output system:
- `pkg/capture/capture.go`
- `pkg/capture/multi_capture.go`
- `pkg/capture/operations.go`
- `pkg/capture/file_retrieval.go`
- `pkg/replay/replay.go`
- `pkg/replay/multi_replay.go`

### Key Improvements
1. **Centralized output logic** - All console output goes through a single, well-tested package
2. **Consistent formatting** - Uniform color scheme and message structure across all commands
3. **Better testability** - Output can be easily mocked/redirected for testing
4. **Cleaner code** - Business logic is no longer mixed with presentation concerns
5. **Future-ready** - Easy to add features like JSON output, quiet mode, or file logging

- [x] Unit tests added for the new output package
- [x] All code compiles without errors
- [x] Manual testing of capture and replay commands

body:
## Did you read the Contributor Guide?

- Yes, I have read the [Contributor Rules](https://sedona.apache.org/latest/community/rule/) and [Contributor Development Guide](https://sedona.apache.org/latest/community/develop/)

## Is this PR related to a ticket?

- Yes, and the PR name follows the format `[GH-XXX] my subject`. Closes #2129

## What changes were proposed in this PR?
This PR refactors all functions implemented in GeoSeries to use Spark's dataframe api instead of Spark SQL. The reasoning is below. Pandas-on-PySpark does not maintain good support for Spark SQL. There are several cases where renaming occurs on either the pandas level or the lower-level spark column level. Previously, we were using `get_first_geometry_column()` to get the name of the column, but this would inaccurately and fails the new `test_complex_df`. I tried using `self.name` in https://github.com/apache/sedona/pull/2130, which was the name on the pandas level and not the spark level that we needed for selectExpr. We now use the built in `self.spark.column` similar to the original library uses, which prevents the need for figuring out the column name.

Two examples of inconsistencies namings that this approach solves:
- `.rename` changes the name on the pandas level but not the spark level
- any operations combining series from different frames (e.g setitem) prepends `__this_` and `__that_` prefixes to the underlying spark columns, without an easy way to fix it.

## How was this patch tested?
Ensured existing tests pass and added a new `test_complex_df` for geodataframe

## Did this PR include necessary documentation updates?

- No, this PR does not affect any public API so no need to change the documentation.

author: robieta
body: Triton calls `inspect.getsource/getsourcelines` a fair amount during compilation. The second call in `JITFunction.__init__` is completely redundant since `getsource` just calls `getsourcelines` under the hood, and caching the source lines on `JITFunction` also lets you skip the calls in `get_jit_fn_file_line`. `getsource` is quite expensive, so this saves >5% of the overall compile time. (Sadly, I think this is the last of the easy compile time wins.)

- Hybrid approach: static YAML + dynamic table providers
- Complete OID management and caching system
- 137 comprehensive tests with full coverage

- **Security**: pg_auth_members, pg_default_acl, pg_init_privs, pg_seclabel

- **Text Search**: pg_ts_config, pg_ts_dict with dynamic registration
- **Statistics**: pg_statistic_ext, pg_statistic_ext_data
- **Replication**: pg_publication_namespace, pg_replication_origin, pg_subscription_rel

author: sasakama-code
body:
## 🤖 Installing Claude Code GitHub App

This PR adds a GitHub Actions workflow that enables Claude Code integration in our repository.

### What is Claude Code?

[Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code) is an AI coding agent that can help with:
- Bug fixes and improvements  
- Documentation updates
- Implementing new features
- Code reviews and suggestions
- Writing tests
- And more!

### How it works

Once this PR is merged, we'll be able to interact with Claude by mentioning @claude in a pull request or issue comment.
Once the workflow is triggered, Claude will analyze the comment and surrounding context, and execute on the request in a GitHub action.

### Important Notes

- **This workflow won't take effect until this PR is merged**
- **@claude mentions won't work until after the merge is complete**
- The workflow runs automatically whenever Claude is mentioned in PR or issue comments
- Claude gets access to the entire PR or issue context including files, diffs, and previous comments

### Security

- Our Anthropic API key is securely stored as a GitHub Actions secret
- Only users with write access to the repository can trigger the workflow
- All Claude runs are stored in the GitHub Actions run history
- Claude's default tools are limited to reading/writing files and interacting with our repo by creating comments, branches, and commits.
- We can add more allowed tools by adding them to the workflow file like:

```
allowed_tools: Bash(npm install),Bash(npm run build),Bash(npm run lint),Bash(npm run test)
```

There's more information in the [Claude Code action repo](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code-action).

After merging this PR, let's try mentioning @claude in a comment on any PR to get started!

Fixes #869

v1.21.0 changed the core challenge flow to maintain information about challenges on the server side instead of only doing them via stateless idempotent generation functions and relying on details to not change. There was a subtle bug introduced in this change: if a client has an unknown challenge ID set in its test cookie, Anubis will clear that cookie and then throw an HTTP 500 error.

This has been fixed by making Anubis throw a new challenge page instead.

author: glecaros
body:
This pull request introduces a significant refactor of the `YamlParser` class to enhance type conversion logic and streamline code readability. The changes include the introduction of a new type conversion system, the removal of redundant logic, and the addition of utility methods for handling YAML scalar values. Additionally, minor formatting adjustments were made in test files for consistency.

### Core Refactor: Type Conversion System
* Introduced a `TypeConverterFactory` to centralize and streamline type conversion logic, replacing scattered type parsing logic in `YamlParser`. (`src/YAYL/YamlParser.cs`, `src/YAYL/conversion/TypeConverterFactory.cs`, [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-b5c18c420e98d20fbb82ce5baf09c80bf4cf326cadcb88594f59caa389c1cb6eL628-R628) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-3e2df09cdfc5e7d9ab3a0d6d4a969dcc44e24f7c6f4b7fbe1b31af797a5a4fcbR1-R90)
* Added individual type converters (`TypeConverter<T>`, `EnumConverter`) to handle specific type parsing, including enums with normalized value names. (`src/YAYL/conversion/TypeConverter.cs`, `src/YAYL/conversion/EnumConverter.cs`, [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-94de1941a6625786bb623eac11ebaad5e6b123e8b41526b5ee53fdd2e81bdf4fR1-R27) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-536cbfad21303c647139faf4cb391ace334c6c877abb4d9c1be2ff3de1275b6cR1-R14)
* Implemented an interface, `ITypeConverter`, to standardize type conversion behavior. (`src/YAYL/conversion/ITypeConverter.cs`, [src/YAYL/conversion/ITypeConverter.csR1-R15](diffhunk://#diff-869115c38026c8296883f51fbaf6b13e4243ffe87f8c7959b067eebbb1bf7275R1-R15))

### Code Simplification and Cleanup
* Removed redundant methods like `NormalizeEnumValueName` and inline logic for type parsing in favor of the new type conversion system. (`src/YAYL/YamlParser.cs`, [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-b5c18c420e98d20fbb82ce5baf09c80bf4cf326cadcb88594f59caa389c1cb6eL73-L74) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-b5c18c420e98d20fbb82ce5baf09c80bf4cf326cadcb88594f59caa389c1cb6eL104-R106) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-b5c18c420e98d20fbb82ce5baf09c80bf4cf326cadcb88594f59caa389c1cb6eL724-R684)
* Replaced hardcoded null value checks with a utility method `GetValue` in `YAMLExtensions`, improving readability and reusability. (`src/YAYL/util/YAMLExtensions.cs`, [src/YAYL/util/YAMLExtensions.csR12-R22](diffhunk://#diff-5aa25f194507c86b7f0c8fd4ecb4981199811d6fda8de715d0f5c639a05a3099R12-R22))

### Utility Enhancements
* Added `GetValue` extension method for `YamlScalarNode` to handle null-like values consistently across the codebase. (`src/YAYL/util/YAMLExtensions.cs`, [src/YAYL/util/YAMLExtensions.csR12-R22](diffhunk://#diff-5aa25f194507c86b7f0c8fd4ecb4981199811d6fda8de715d0f5c639a05a3099R12-R22))

### Test Adjustments
* Reformatted lambda expressions in test files for consistent code style. (`test/YAYL.Tests/YamlParserTests.Files.cs`, `test/YAYL.Tests/YamlParserTests.cs`, [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-8d93867ca4dc497aeeb8650467899609d0a5d2bc4a7090dfea866adef5f79cbfL115-R121) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-5e0ee8f447594108a92678f9ffe624d9dffbd739cae1cc3a8fe1c1c6ddec04f9L476-R477) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-5e0ee8f447594108a92678f9ffe624d9dffbd739cae1cc3a8fe1c1c6ddec04f9L494-R496)

author: do5-5anto5
body:
This PR introduces the new `ChangeStateMixin`, a powerful solution designed to streamline both simple and complex state management within our applications. This mixin provides flexible and efficient ways to handle UI states, ensuring automatic cleanup and improved performance.

---

### Key Features

* **Complex State Management with `useChangeState()`**: For intricate UI states, `useChangeState()` offers a robust and comprehensive approach. It's designed to handle scenarios where multiple interdependencies and sophisticated logic are required.
* **Simple State Management with `useStateObservable()`**: For straightforward state needs, `useStateObservable()` provides a lightweight and efficient alternative. This is ideal for managing individual values or simple UI toggles.
* **Automatic Listener Cleanup**: The mixin ensures **automatic cleanup of listeners** when the associated widget is disposed. This eliminates memory leaks and reduces boilerplate code, leading to more stable and performant applications.

author: movm
body:
## Summary
- Implements focus-aware autosave system that eliminates visual flashing and user interruption
- Replaces polling-based autosave (500ms intervals) with event-driven approach
- Creates shared `useAutosave` hook for all profile components

## Key Improvements
- **No more flashing**: Removed `disabled={isSaving}` states that caused form inputs to flash
- **Focus-aware**: Prevents saves while user is actively typing in form fields
- **Efficient API calls**: Only saves fields that actually changed (field-level tracking)
- **Better performance**: Event-driven triggers instead of aggressive polling intervals
- **Industry standard**: Users can type continuously without interruption during background saves

## Components Updated
- ✅ `IntelligenceTab.jsx` - Now uses shared autosave hook
- ✅ `GroupsManagementTab.jsx` - Removed visual flashing during saves
- ✅ `AnweisungenWissenTab.jsx` - Focus-aware autosave implementation
- ✅ `ProfileInfoTab.jsx` - Enhanced state-based autosave pattern

## Technical Changes
- **New**: `useAutosave.js` - Shared hook with focus detection and field-level change tracking
- **Improved**: 2000ms debounce delay (was 1000ms) for better performance
- **Preserved**: Delete operation loading states and other appropriate disabled states
- **Removed**: All `disabled={isSaving}` props from form inputs that should stay interactive

## Test Plan
- [ ] Navigate to profile sections and verify no visual flashing during autosave
- [ ] Type in form fields continuously - should not be interrupted by saves
- [ ] Verify changes are still saved automatically in background
- [ ] Test delete operations still show appropriate loading states
- [ ] Confirm focus detection works (no saves while actively typing)
